source.title: Compositional structure can emerge without generational transmission

confidence_rationale: This is the strongest single piece of evidence in this pull for any ARC-099 inventory item, and it was not on the radar when the Galke et al. 2022 entry was written. Study 2 is a 24-group meta-analysis that competes the two candidate compressibility pressures against each other and finds that NUMBER OF PARTNERS drives compositional structure (beta = 0.04, SE = 0.006, t = 6.37, p < 0.001) while the expanding meaning space does not add a unique contribution (beta = 0.0001, t = 0.04, p = 0.96; model comparison dAIC = 2, p = 0.96 against the partners-only model). ARC-099 lists partner variation as an enabling condition; here it is measured directly, as the manipulated variable rather than as a held-constant feature of the paradigm, and it survives competition. Study 1 separately establishes that compositional structure emerges within a single generation of four people, so generational transmission -- and with it the transmission-side memory bottleneck that Kirby et al. 2015 had argued was necessary -- is not required. Confidence 0.84 rather than higher because Study 2 is a meta-analysis across groups run under two protocol lengths rather than a within-design manipulation of partner number, and because the mapping to a V6 ecology remains an analogy.
failure_signatures: The expanding meaning space -- an obvious candidate for 'coordination pressure' operationalised as referential load -- had NO unique effect on structure once number of partners was in the model (beta = 0.0001, p = 0.96). A V6 ecology that grows its referent set to create structure pressure, without growing the number of distinct interaction partners, is pulling the lever this experiment found inert.

Kirby, Tamariz, Cornish and Smith (2015) had argued compositional languages emerge ONLY across generations. That is falsified here within a single generation. Any V6-entry contract that inherits a generational-transmission requirement -- or that treats a learner-side transmission bottleneck as the necessary source of compressibility pressure -- inherits a claim this experiment overturned.

The authors locate compressibility pressure in 'participants' limited memory capacity', but explicitly say such limitations 'can stem from different sources': transmission-side learning constraints OR the communicative need to converge with many partners. Bounded memory is therefore a FUNCTIONAL requirement satisfiable by more than one ecology configuration, not a substrate property to be checked off. An inventory item phrased as 'bounded memory' would be under-determined in exactly the way ARC-099's partner-variation item currently is.

Structure rose linearly over rounds with the quadratic term non-significant, unlike the 2019 Proc B study where it was non-linear and decelerating. The time-course of emergence is not stable across protocol lengths, so a V6 probe with a fixed episode budget may read a real effect as absent purely because it sampled the wrong stretch.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Compositional languages can emerge in a closed community within a single generation, without transmission to new learners, when communication includes two real-world compressibility pressures: multiple interaction partners and an expanding meaning space. Study 1 (24 adults, six four-person micro-societies) shows structure increases significantly and linearly over rounds. Study 2, a meta-analysis over 24 groups, competes the two pressures and finds that number of partners has a strong effect on structure while number of scenes does not add a unique contribution.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-099 lists partner variation among fourteen jointly-necessary enabling conditions. Study 2 is the closest thing in this literature to a direct test of that item, and it passes: with both candidate pressures in one model over 24 groups, partner number carries the effect and the expanding meaning space does not. This upgrades partner variation from a plausible listing to the best-evidenced item in the inventory, and it does so with a measured competition rather than an appeal to a paradigm feature. It also settles part of the bounded-memory question the Galke et al. 2022 entry opened. Kirby et al. 2015 had argued compositional structure requires transmission across generations -- i.e. that the compressibility pressure must come from a learner-side bottleneck. This paper falsifies the necessity half of that within a single generation, and the authors' own framing is the useful one for REE: compressibility pressure arises from limited memory capacity, but that pressure 'can stem from different sources' -- learning constraints in transmission, or the need to converge with many partners in communication. Translated to a V6 contract, the checkable condition is a compressibility pressure with a named source, not a substrate flag reading 'memory is bounded'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Study 2 is a meta-analysis over groups that were run under two different protocol lengths (16 rounds and a shorter 8-round version) and two group sizes, not a within-experiment manipulation of partner number; number of partners is therefore partly confounded with group size and with how long a group ran. The authors are explicit that this is a meta-analysis and report the model comparison rather than claiming an experimental dissociation. Separately, 'number of partners' here ranges over small integers (a four-person closed group gives each participant three partners; an eight-person group, seven) -- nothing establishes what happens at ecology scale. And as with every entry in this directory, the participants are adults who already possess language; the study tells REE what ecology conditions elicit structure from capable agents, not whether ARC-099's substrate inventory is complete.
mapping.source_context: Study 1: 24 Dutch-speaking adults (mean age 23.2), six closed micro-societies of four, alternating dyads, typed artificial labels for visual scenes, expanding meaning space. Study 2: meta-analysis over 24 groups (the six from Study 1 plus 18 run on an extended version -- six of four members, twelve of eight), modelling structure score against number of partners and number of scenes.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.84: peer-reviewed Cognition paper, two studies, 24 groups in the pooled analysis, mixed-effects models with reported model comparisons, and a result that directly contradicts a prior high-profile claim (Kirby et al. 2015) rather than confirming the field's expectation -- which is the kind of finding least likely to be a file-drawer artefact. Mapping fidelity 0.80, the highest of the primary entries in this directory, because Study 2's dependent variable is the emergence of compositional structure and its competing predictors are two candidate ENABLING CONDITIONS -- structurally the same question ARC-099 asks. Transfer risk 0.38: lower than the other human entries because what transfers here is a claim about which ecology property drives structure, which is more portable than a claim about human cognition, but non-zero because partner number in a four-to-eight person closed group is a long way from an artificial ecology's notion of a partner.
